\section{Hypercontractivity --- Cube --- Foundations}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.Basic
\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Cube --- Foundations: Introduction}
Uniform-cube event probabilities, variance, Fourier influence bounds, and real-exponent power means are developed here. The module supplies moment interpolation, tail bounds, and scalar estimates used in hypercontractive applications.

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Cube --- Foundations: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier coefficients of coordinate derivatives]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourierCoeff_derivative}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_add, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_neg, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_false, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_true, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.chiS_flipBit_eq, BooleanAnalysis.derivative, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.flipBit, BooleanAnalysis.flipBit_flipBit, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p047-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p047-b008
}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$, $i\in[n]$, and $S\subseteq[n]$. For the signed coordinate derivative $D_i f(x)=\tfrac12(-1)^{x_i}(f(x)-f(x^{\oplus i}))$, where $x^{\oplus i}$ flips coordinate $i$, one has $\widehat{D_i f}(S)=0$ if $i\in S$, and $\widehat{D_i f}(S)=\widehat f(S\cup\{i\})$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Subtracting constants preserves degree]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.has_degree_at_most_sub_const}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_sub, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.chiS_empty, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.fourier_coeff_chi, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fourier degree at most $k$, where $n,k\in\mathbb N$,
and let $c\in\mathbb R$. Then the function $x\mapsto f(x)-c$ has Fourier degree at most
$k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Cube event indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p029-b004}
For an event $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, its indicator $\mathbf1_A$ is the real-valued function equal to $1$ on $A$ and $0$ outside $A$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform cube probability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeProbability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
For an event $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, define its uniform probability by $\Pr[A]=\E[\mathbf1_A]=2^{-n}|A|$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Variance on the cube]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p018-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p027-b001
}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$, define $\operatorname{Var}(f)=\E[(f-\E f)^2]$, with uniform expectation on the cube.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
For every $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, its variance under the uniform measure on the
Boolean cube is the sum of the squared Fourier–Walsh coefficients over all nonempty
subsets of coordinates: $\operatorname{Var}(f)=\sum_{\varnothing\ne
S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Degree bound for total influence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.totalInfluence_le_degree_mul_variance}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_eq_sum_nonempty_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fourier degree at most $k$.
Then its total influence satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^n\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\le
k\,\operatorname{Var}(f)$, with variance and coordinate influences taken under the
uniform measure on the cube.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Squared influences under a degree bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_sq_influences_le_degree_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.totalInfluence_le_degree_mul_variance, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p048-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p052-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p052-b003
}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ have Fourier degree at most $k$, variance at most $1$, and coordinate influences $\operatorname{Inf}_i(f)\le\varepsilon$ for every $i$, where $\varepsilon\ge0$. Then $\sum_i\operatorname{Inf}_i(f)^2\le k\varepsilon$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Variance and noisy Fourier energy]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_rpow_ratio_le_noisy_total}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteNorms.weighted_rpow_mean_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_eq_sum_nonempty_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have positive variance under the uniform measure, and let
$\rho>0$. If $I(f)$ is the sum of the coordinate influences and $\widehat f(S)$ are the
Fourier–Walsh coefficients, then
$\operatorname{Var}(f)\,\rho^{I(f)/\operatorname{Var}(f)}\leq\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|S|\rho^{|S|}\widehat
f(S)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Real-exponent cube power mean]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
Let $p\in\bbr$ and $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$, define $\|f\|_p=(\E|f|^p)^{1/p}$ using real powers and uniform expectation, with $1/0=0$, $a^0=1$ for $a\ge0$, and $0^r=0$ for $r\ne0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Second power mean and second norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm_two}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm}
\difficulty{1}
For every $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, its power mean of order two under the uniform
measure equals its $L^2$ norm: $(\mathbb E|f|^2)^{1/2}=\sqrt{\mathbb E[f^2]}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recovering the absolute moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and let $q>0$. For the power mean $\|f\|_q=(\mathbb
E|f|^q)^{1/q}$ under the uniform measure on the Boolean cube, $\|f\|_q^q=\mathbb
E|f|^q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Moment tail bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeProbability_le_cubeLpNorm_div_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm_rpow, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeProbability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_mono, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and let $q,c>0$. Under the uniform measure on the Boolean
cube, $\Pr(|f(x)|\geq c)\leq(\|f\|_q/c)^q$, where $\|f\|_q=(\mathbb E|f|^q)^{1/q}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Interpolation of Cube Moments]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cube_moment_interpolation}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and let $p,q\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<p<2<q$. With
expectation taken uniformly on the cube, $\mathbb E[f^2]\le (\mathbb
E|f|^p)^{(q-2)/(q-p)}(\mathbb E|f|^q)^{(2-p)/(q-p)}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Scalar interpolation cancellation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lp_interpolation_cancel}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $A,M,u,v,c\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $A\ge0$, $M>0$, $u>0$, and $u+v=2$. If $M^2\le
A^u(e^cM)^v$, then $M\le e^{cv/u}A$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Norm Comparison by Interpolation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cube_norm_interpolation_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm_rpow, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cube_moment_interpolation, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lp_interpolation_cancel, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct_self_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $p,q,c\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<p<2<q$. If
$\|f\|_q\le e^c\|f\|_2$, then $\|f\|_2\le
\exp\!\left(\frac{cq(2-p)}{p(q-2)}\right)\|f\|_p$, where the power means use uniform
expectation on the cube.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Positive-event bound for centered functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.centered_abs_expect_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeProbability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_sub, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct}
\difficulty{4}
Let $g$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ with uniform mean
zero. Then $(\mathbb E|g|)^2\leq4\langle g,g\rangle\Pr[g>0]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indicator pairing from an exponential moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.indicator_innerProduct_le_of_mgf}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_add, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_mono, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, with $f$ taking only the values $0$ and $1$, and
suppose its uniform expectation $\alpha=\mathbb E f$ is positive. For any $t,b\in\mathbb
R$, if $\mathbb E e^{tg}\le e^b$, then $t\,\mathbb
E[fg]\le\alpha\bigl(b-\log\alpha\bigr)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise operator bound for bounded-degree functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.l2Norm_noiseOp_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.parseval}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k$ be natural numbers and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fourier degree at
most $k$, meaning every nonzero Fourier coefficient is indexed by a set of size at most
$k$. For every real $\rho\ge1$, the $L^2$ norm under the uniform measure satisfies
$\|T_\rho f\|_2\le\rho^k\|f\|_2$, where $T_\rho$ multiplies the Fourier coefficient at
each set $S$ by $\rho^{|S|}$.
\end{lemma}

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Cube --- Foundations: Further results}

\begin{lemma}[Three-halves influence bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_three_halves_influences_le_degree_mul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_three_halves_influences_le_degree_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.totalInfluence_le_degree_mul_variance, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fourier degree at most $k$
and variance at most $1$ under the uniform measure. Suppose
$\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\le\varepsilon$ for every coordinate $i$, where $\varepsilon\in\mathbb
R$. Then $\sum_{i=1}^n\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]^{3/2}\le k\sqrt{\varepsilon}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise decreases cube variance]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_noiseOp_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_noiseOp_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_eq_sum_nonempty_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and $0\leq\rho\leq1$. For the Fourier noise operator
$T_\rho$, the variance under the uniform measure satisfies $\operatorname{Var}(T_\rho
f)\leq\operatorname{Var}(f)$.
\end{lemma}
